| [NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md) | The Homological Nature of Entropy | On a finite probability space, take an information structure S (a set of partitions closed under joins that have a common refinement in S and containing the trivial partition) and a probability family Q complete for it. If S is connected and "sufficiently rich" and cochains are measurable, then H¹ is one-dimensional and spanned by Shannon entropy (Thm 1). This makes entropy the unique measurable 1-cocycle, up to one multiplicative constant per connected component. Theorem 5 gives a Blahut–Arimoto-style alternating iteration that converges but, being non-convex jointly, not necessarily to a unique solution. | Read |
| [NOTE-306](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-306.md) v3 | Information-theoretic analysis of generalization capability of learning algorithms | If the loss ℓ(w,Z) is σ-subgaussian for every w, then the expected generalisation error of any learning algorithm P_{W\|S} obeys \|E[L_μ(W) − L_S(W)]\| ≤ √(2σ²·I(S;W)/n) (Theorem 1). This extends Russo–Zou to uncountable hypothesis spaces, and the paper adds a high-probability version, n = (8σ²/α²)(ε/β + log(2/β)) (Theorem 3). Minimising empirical risk plus I(S;W), relaxed to a KL term against a prior Q, yields exactly the Gibbs algorithm (Theorem 5). Noisy ERM and adaptive composition are analysed through the same mutual-information quantity. | Read |
| [NOTE-308](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-308.md) | How much does your data exploration overfit? Controlling bias via information usage | Suppose an analyst reports statistic φ_T, chosen by any data-dependent rule T from m candidates each σ-sub-Gaussian. Then the selection bias obeys \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) (Prop. 1), where "information usage" I(T;φ) ≤ H(T) ≤ log m. For argmax selection over φ ~ N(µ,I) the squared error is Θ(1 + H(T)) (Prop. 3). Adaptive analyses compose additively, with I(T_{k+1};φ) ≤ Σ_i I(Y_{T_i};φ_{T_i} \| H_{i−1},T_i) (Lemma 1). Answering each query with Gaussian noise of variance σ²√j/n therefore keeps the k-th answer's error at O(σk^{1/4}/√n) (Prop. 7). | Read |
| [NOTE-310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-310.md) | Notes on Landauer's principle, reversible computation, and Maxwell's Demon | Bennett states Landauer's principle as a consequence of the Second Law. A logically irreversible step, meaning erasure or a *merge of control flow*, must export at least the lost entropy (k ln 2 per bit) to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom. That export need not take the form of heat (p. 1). Logically reversible operations, including copying onto a blank register and measurement, have no minimum cost. He calls "an intrinsic cost of order kT for every elementary act of information processing" a 20th-century "misconception" (pp. 5–6). Erasing random data can itself be thermodynamically reversible; the waste comes from applying a many-to-one operation to *known* data (pp. 1, 4). | Read |
| [NOTE-315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-315.md) | The Theory of Signal Detectability. Part I: The General Theory; Part II: Applications with Gaussian Noise | Peterson and Birdsall show that the criterion approach (maximise P_SN(A) − β·P_N(A), or maximise detection at fixed false-alarm k) and the Woodward–Davies a-posteriori approach are all solved by one receiver that computes the likelihood ratio ℓ(x) = f_SN(x)/f_N(x) and thresholds it (Part I, Theorems 1–7). They introduce the receiver operating characteristic, whose slope at each point is the threshold β (Theorem 8, Eq. 2.51). For a signal known exactly in white Gaussian noise, ln ℓ is normal with equal variance 2E/N₀ under both hypotheses and means 2E/N₀ apart, so the ROC is a one-parameter family indexed by the "detection index" d = (M_SN − M_N)²/σ² = 2E/N₀ (Part II, Eqs. 4.1–4.8, Fig. 4.1). The receiver is a correlator or matched filter (Eq. 5.3, 4.10). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-320](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-320.md) v2 | On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning | Replicating Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby with their own code, the paper shows the information-plane "compression phase" appears only for double-saturating nonlinearities measured through an imposed binning/noise model: tanh compresses, ReLU/softplus/linear do not (binning, KDE, Kraskov; SZT task and MNIST), and re-binning the same tanh run evenly in net input removes it. Compression and generalisation dissociate in all four combinations, full-batch GD compresses as much as SGD, and the drift→diffusion gradient-SNR transition occurs in networks that cannot compress (ReLU, MNIST, a 1-1-1 linear net), so it is real but unrelated to compression. | Read |
| [NOTE-325](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-325.md) | On Context-Content Uncertainty Principle | The paper assumes structured content has far lower entropy than context, H(Φ) ≪ H(Ψ), and from the chain rule H(Φ,Ψ) = H(Φ) + H(Ψ\|Φ) concludes that inference should establish content first and then resolve context. It then derives four layers of "operational principles" and a reading of five brain theories as instances. The principles cover attention, learning rates, memory, staged learning and hierarchy. All of this is argued, not shown. There are no experiments, the abstract's simulations are absent, and the proofs of Theorems 1, 3 and 6–8 are wrong as written. | Read |
| [NOTE-365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-365.md) | Integrated Information Theory 3.0 | The 2014 restatement of IIT. Five axioms of experience become five postulates about mechanisms in a state, and an experience is identified with the maximally irreducible conceptual structure of a complex. Exclusion is the anti-nesting rule: of all overlapping sets of elements, only the one with locally maximal Φ is conscious, so no subset or superset of a complex is. It is postulated from the axiom that experience has definite borders; Occam's razor is invoked only for exclusion within a mechanism. Logic-gate examples give minor complexes, a conscious inactive network, a minimally conscious photodiode and a feed-forward zombie. Nothing larger than about a dozen elements is computable. | Read |
| [NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md) | Entropy production fluctuation theorem and the nonequilibrium work relation for free energy differences | A finite-time fluctuation theorem for stochastic dynamics. If the dynamics are Markovian and microscopically reversible (path over reversed path = e^{−βQ}) and the entropy production ω = ln ρ(x_{−τ}) − ln ρ(x_{+τ}) − βQ is odd under time reversal, then P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^{ω}. For processes that start and end in equilibrium ω = β(W − ΔF), so the Jarzynski equality is one line. For time-symmetric steady states, P(+ω)/P(−ω) = e^{ω} for any whole number of cycles. At long times it gives a heat fluctuation theorem and Gaussians with variance twice the mean. | Read |
| [NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md) | Stochastic thermodynamics, fluctuation theorems and molecular machines | The 2012 reference review of stochastic thermodynamics. For Markovian dynamics coupled to baths of fixed temperature, work, heat and a stochastic entropy s = −ln p(x(τ),τ) are defined on single trajectories. Every known integral, detailed and Crooks-type fluctuation theorem follows from one master theorem, as the log-ratio of a path's weight under the original and a conjugate dynamics. Dissipation measures how distinguishable forward and reverse paths are. Feedback adds the mutual information I to the second law (Sagawa–Ueda). Machine efficiency and efficiency at maximum power follow from a cycle decomposition. The integral theorems are not proofs of the second law, because the dynamics build irreversibility in. | Read |
| [NOTE-422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-422.md) | Comments on a derivation and application of the ‘maximum entropy production’ principle | Two corrections to Dewar. First, Dewar 2005 derives MaxEP far from equilibrium from a fluctuation theorem plus a quadratic approximation to the flux distribution, used as if valid for all f. Both can hold together only for small F, where A(F) = ∂λ/∂F is constant: the linear regime. So the orthogonality condition ∂D/∂F = 4λ, which yields both maximum and minimum dissipation, fails for nonlinear constitutive relations, as an exactly solvable spin chain shows. Second, Dewar 2003's SOC divergence disappears once the quartic term is kept. | Read |
| [NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md) | Information theory explanation of the fluctuation theorem, maximum entropy production and self-organized criticality in non-equilibrium stationary states | Jaynes's maximum-entropy inference, applied to microscopic paths of an open stationary system, gives p_Γ = exp(A_Γ)/Z. The action is a symmetric end-point term plus τσ_Γ/2k_B. A fluctuation theorem p(σ) = e^{τσ/k_B} p(−σ) and ⟨σ⟩ ≥ 0 follow exactly. Maximum entropy production follows only in a mean-field approximation, and only if the number of paths increases with their irreversible action, which is assumed. The self-organized-criticality corollary is a mean-field divergence. As Grinstein and Linsker showed, it does not survive keeping the quartic term. | Read |
| [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) | Sophisticated Inference | Expected free energy evaluated recursively over the beliefs an agent would hold after each plausible outcome turns active inference into a pruned tree search over belief states, formally analogous to Bellman recursion. Small simulations show it planning through short-term costs (an aversive cue; a maze barrier needing horizon four) and exploring by novelty. Its scalability is argued from pruning, not demonstrated; its first-principles grounding is cited, not developed. | Read |
| [NOTE-476](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-476.md) | Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training | NC1 Σ_W → 0 (Tr(Σ_WΣ_B†)/C falls), NC2 centred means → simplex ETF (cosines → −1/(C−1)), NC3 W ∝ Ṁᵀ, NC4 nearest class mean; 7 datasets × 3 nets, 480 models. Median TPT gains: +0.35 points test accuracy, +0.0252 DeepFool robustness. NC1–2 ⇒ NC3–4 for Webb–Lowe and max-margin (Theorems 2, 4). Optimal small-noise error exponent C/(C−1)·1/4, only at simplex ETFs (Theorem 5). | Read |
| [NOTE-591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md) | A Mathematical Theory of Communication | Shannon defines a discrete source as an ergodic Markov process and its information rate as H = −Σ p log p per symbol, proves that typical long sequences number about 2^{HN} (Theorems 3–4) and that a source can be sent over a noiseless channel at C/H − ε symbols per second and no faster (Theorem 9). For a noisy channel he defines R = H(x) − H_y(x) and C = max R, and proves by averaging over random codes that any rate below C can be sent with arbitrarily small error frequency, while above C the equivocation is at least H − C (Theorem 11). The continuous parts add the sampling representation, C = W log(1 + P/N) for white noise, and a minimum rate for a source at a given fidelity. | Read |
| [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md) | Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments | Gives a new minimax proof of the Sherman–Stein theorem (for finite outcome spaces, an experiment at least as informative as another in every decision problem can reproduce it by a Markov matrix) and, by a martingale argument, removes the finiteness restriction, so for a finite parameter set "more informative" and "sufficient for" coincide in general. Adds k-decision problems, with three equivalent forms, and shows that for dichotomies two-action problems, and so the type I/type II error trade-off, already decide the order. | Read |
| [NOTE-605](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-605.md) | Rate-Distortion-Perception Theory for Semantic Communication | Formulates semantic communication as indirect source coding of a hidden source S, observed by the encoder only through X, with decoder side information, common randomness, an expected-distortion constraint on S and a total-variation constraint on the law of the reconstruction. States a rate region (proof sketched) and a binary closed form, showing that perfect recovery of X does not recover S and that side information alone can meet loose constraints at zero rate. | Read |
| [NOTE-619](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-619.md) | Semantic Communication: A Survey of Its Theoretical Development | Surveys semantic information theory around three Shannon analogues: semantic entropy (no agreed definition; logical-probability, task, knowledge and context variants), semantic rate–distortion (meaning as a latent state S behind the observation X, with dual distortions), and semantic channel capacity (definitions under which it can exceed Shannon capacity). It adds the information bottleneck, age of information, joint source–channel coding and LLMs as tools, and lists open problems. It catalogues rather than reconciles. | Read |
| [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md) | Informative communication in word production and word learning | Writes the informative speaker down: utility is −D_KL(intended meaning ‖ literal word meaning), so a speaker referring to one object picks a true word with probability ∝ \|extension\|^(−α), the size principle from communicative premises. Learners who know the referent and invert this speaker bet on novel-word meanings as predicted (r = .93); speakers' free descriptions follow informativeness only weakly (r = .19), and colour terms not at all. | Read |
| [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md) | Efficient compression in color naming | Casts a colour lexicon as an information-bottleneck encoder from perceptual meanings to words and shows the World Color Survey languages and English lie near the IB bound at β ≈ 1.03, beating hue-rotated variants of themselves in 93% of cases and fitting full naming distributions much better than a deterministic efficiency model; IB optima are soft, and the path of optima through β has phase transitions that roughly follow Berlin and Kay's sequence. | Read |
| [NOTE-638](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-638.md) | Semantic Rate-Distortion Theory with Applications | Defines semantic distortion between the posterior of a latent meaning given the original and given the reconstructed observation, and proves that the resulting information rate–distortion function, with a second symbolic constraint, is the operational limit under lower semicontinuity; solves the binary symmetric case. Its sequence distortion is defined as an expected maximum but the proofs use maxima of expectations; with KL divergence the function is the information bottleneck, which the paper does not note. | Read |
| [NOTE-668](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-668.md) | Hippocampal spatial representations exhibit a hyperbolic geometry | In rat dorsal CA1, the rank order of pairwise spike correlations matches points drawn uniformly from a 3D hyperbolic ball, not from a low-dimensional Euclidean cube, and the ball's radius grows with the logarithm of exploration time. Place-field sizes are near exponential, which a Poisson model shows is more informative than uniform or log-normal sizes. The evidence separates "hyperbolic ball, uniform" from "Euclidean cube, uniform"; it does not separate a hyperbolic metric from an exponential distribution of field sizes, and the hierarchy it describes is nesting of field scales, not a recovered tree. | Read |
| [NOTE-674](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-674.md) | Mutual information, neural networks and the renormalization group | Makes "the relevant degrees of freedom" of real-space RG an optimizable quantity: the coarse variable of a block that carries the most mutual information about the system beyond a buffer. Learned from Monte Carlo samples, it recovers Kadanoff block spins for 2D Ising and the electric-field variables of the dimer model, discards decoupled noise, and, iterated, gives the Ising flow and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a distribution-fitting RBM keeps the noise. The equivalence with a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is shown only for 1D and quasi-1D. | Read |
| [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md) | Generalized Information-Theoretic Tree Abstractions (G-tree search) | Proves that when the encoder is a pruning of a fixed quadtree, any weighted sum of relevant-information, irrelevant-information and compression terms splits over interior nodes, so a bottom-up recursion finds the optimal tree with fewest leaves exactly, in linear time, where greedy splitting can miss everything. The tree solving IB with side information is always a pruning of the plain IB tree for the same β. | Read |
| [NOTE-681](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-681.md) v2 | Statistical Physics through the Lens of Real-Space Mutual Information | Makes the real-space mutual-information principle a single-shot operator finder: a CNN coarse-graining co-trained against a neural InfoNCE bound, optimized once at a large buffer, returns on the interacting dimer model the order parameters below the BKT transition and the electric fields above it, and one fitted scaling dimension (1.00037 against 1). The maximal information is log 4 in the ordered phase and decays algebraically with the buffer in the critical one. The model's operators were known; the optimality theorem is cited. | Read |
| [NOTE-682](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-682.md) | Optimal Renormalization Group Transformation from Information Theory | Proves that a block coarse-graining keeping all of the block's mutual information with the system beyond a buffer makes the coarse measure factorize across the block, so a finite-range Hamiltonian gains no range (1D; D dimensions with an extra assumption) and 1D disorder gains no correlations across it. Where the condition fails, as it does for its own examples, it shows on two-spin blocks of 1D Ising chains that longer-range, many-spin and disorder-correlation terms shrink as more information is kept. Explains decimation in 1D and majority rule in 2D by the cost of encoding into one binary spin. | Read |
| [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md) | Deriving neural scaling laws from language statistics | Predicts the data-limited scaling exponent of language-model test loss as γ/(2β), from two measured corpus statistics: the decay with lag of the top singular value of the token–token covariance (β), which sets the usable context n*(P) ~ P^(1/(2β)), and the decay of next-token conditional entropy with context (γ). The derivation rests on assumed scaling forms and a fast-learning condition; on TinyStories and WikiText-103 transformers match the predicted exponents up to about 10^8 tokens and horizons of a few tens of tokens. | Read |
| [NOTE-690](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-690.md) | Relevance in the Renormalization Group and in Information Theory | Proves, for a short-range lattice model on a cylinder with block and environment as slabs separated by a buffer, that the information- bottleneck encoder at its first transition depends on the block only through the boundary weak value of the leading transfer-matrix eigenvector, which at large circumference is the lowest-dimension primary, with β_c = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B); checked on a three-site Ising cylinder. It does not cover the planar block-in-a-shell geometry or the fixed-alphabet β → ∞ limit that RSMI uses, which [LIT-878](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-878.md) relies on. | Read |
| [NOTE-692](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-692.md) v2 | Symmetries and phase diagrams with real-space mutual information neural estimation | The long companion of [LIT-878](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-878.md). Derives the RSMI-NE estimator and shows that the maximal real-space information counts ordered sectors (1 bit for the Ising ferromagnet, 2 for columnar dimers), decays exponentially with the buffer off criticality and algebraically at it, and that the ensemble of optimal filters from independent runs maps a degenerate subspace whose projections show broken lattice symmetries and the dimers' emergent U(1). All the models' answers were known; the non-equilibrium example is one figure. | Read |
| [NOTE-717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-717.md) | Kamenica & Gentzkow — Bayesian Persuasion | With a common prior and a sender who commits to a signal the receiver sees, any distribution of posteriors whose mean is the prior can be induced, so the sender's best value is the concave closure of its posterior-value function at the prior (Corollary 2). A fully informed, fully rational receiver can be moved; at the optimum she is indifferent whenever she acts for the sender. The paper never cites Blackwell, does not analyse manipulation, and has the receiver know the design. | Read |
| [NOTE-718](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-718.md) | Gallego & Orús — Language Design as Information Renormalization | Reads Chomsky's MERGE as a coarse-graining and builds sentence probabilities as mostly loop-free tensor networks of 3-index MERGE tensors, one per node of a given parse. Because MERGE's output is fixed by its input, a parsed sentence's probability is a product of local coefficients. Tree-shaped parses make correlations decay with tree distance, about log \|j − i\|, so polynomially in word separation. The averaging step that turns this into a claim about languages is asserted, and nothing is tested on data. Syntax only: semantics and context are set aside by the authors. | Read |
| [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md) | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi — Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro | Effective information (EI), the mutual information between uniformly imposed interventions on a system's states and their effects, can be higher for a coarse-grained macro description than for the micro description it supervenes on. This happens when coarse-graining makes the mechanisms more deterministic or less degenerate by more than the smaller state space costs. Four toy systems of binary logic gates give gains of 0.40 to 2.92 bits. Causal emergence is defined as that gain. The examples are computed exactly; the reading of the EI peak as the level where causation happens rests on the choice of a uniform intervention distribution at each level, which the paper adopts and does not test. | Read |
| [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md) v2 | Poole et al. — On Variational Bounds of Mutual Information | The common variational lower bounds on mutual information (Barber–Agakov, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE, InfoNCE) are derived from one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound. InfoNCE is the multi-sample NWJ bound with the batch mean as its partition estimate, which proves it a lower bound for every critic when the K pairs are i.i.d.; it is capped at log K. An interpolated family I_α trades InfoNCE's bias against NWJ's variance, and none of them gives low bias and low variance when MI is large and the batch small. | Read |
| [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md) | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski — MDL and Generalization Guarantees for Representation Learning | The expected generalisation error of an encoder–decoder classifier is bounded by 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is a KL divergence between the encoder's joint law of train-and-ghost latents and a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations. The bound holds for any decoder, stays finite for deterministic continuous encoders under lossy compression, and is never evaluated numerically. A VIB variant with label-dependent learned priors gains about 2.5 points on CIFAR-10. | Read |
| [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md) | Tschannen et al. — On Mutual Information Maximization for Representation Learning | Four controlled experiments on MNIST image halves (two repeated on CIFAR10) show that downstream linear accuracy of InfoNCE- and NWJ-trained encoders does not track mutual information. Invertible encoders improve while true MI is constant. Higher NWJ bounds from an MLP critic give worse features. At matched bound values, ConvNets beat MLPs. The paper also proves that InfoNCE is neither a lower nor an upper bound on MI when batch pairs are dependent, and recasts it as a multi-class K-pair metric learning loss. | Read |
| [NOTE-754](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-754.md) | Fischer — The Conditional Entropy Bottleneck | The MNI criterion asks for I(X;Y) = I(X;Z) = I(Y;Z), and CEB targets it by minimizing I(X;Z\|Y) − γI(Y;Z), which is IB with γ = β − 1. CEB beats VIB at every ρ on Fashion MNIST for accuracy and robustness, and a CEB Wide ResNet beats Madry's adversarially trained model on CIFAR-10 without adversarial training. That retained information causes the robustness failures is a hypothesis, supported only by these experiments. | Read |
| [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md) | Varley — Flickering Emergences | Information-theoretic emergence measures built on past–future mutual information are expected values, and their local (pointwise) values can be negative. In a four-node Boolean toy, a coarse-graining that is emergent on average maps about 53% of informative micro transitions to misinformative macro ones, and the whole-to-whole synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of macro transitions. In a connectome, misinformative edges fall mostly between communities. The paper argues the possibility is general to any excess-entropy measure; it shows instances, not a theorem. | Read |
| [NOTE-760](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-760.md) | Grünwald & Roos — Minimum Description Length Revisited | A review of MDL since 2007. Each model is replaced by one universal distribution, chosen for small worst-case log-loss regret against the model's best fit. NML is the minimax choice, with complexity (k/2) log(n/2π) + log ∫ v√\|I\| + o(1). Estimation is penalised ML with a luckiness function v. The switch distribution nearly resolves AIC–BIC, the RIPr gives tests safe under optional continuation, and MDL and Bayes can be inconsistent under misspecification. Results are cited, not proved. | Read |
| [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md) | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman — A measure for brain complexity | Defines neural complexity C_N as the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear increase with subset size, equivalently the average mutual information across bipartitions summed over sizes. It is zero for independent parts, low for uniformly dependent ones and high when the two coexist. In simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity gives higher C_N than the same connections spread randomly. One number for a whole system, with no partition, threshold or penalty. | Read |
| [NOTE-776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-776.md) | Grünwald & Vitányi — Shannon information and Kolmogorov complexity | A survey pairing Shannon's and Kolmogorov's notions. Expected Kolmogorov complexity exceeds entropy by between 0 and K(f) + O(1), and expected algorithmic mutual information lies between I(X;Y) − K(f) and I(X;Y) + 2K(f). An algorithmic sufficient statistic is probabilistically nearly sufficient in expectation, one way only. The expected structure function brackets the distortion-rate function with a K(f, d, m, R) shift in rate. Each link holds only up to the complexity of the distribution. | Read |
| [NOTE-780](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-780.md) | Sefidgaran, Gohari, Richard & Şimşekli — Rate-Distortion Theoretic Generalization Bounds | The expected generalisation error of any algorithm is at most √(2σ²·R/n) + ε, where R is the least mutual information I(S;Ŵ) of any surrogate output whose expected generalisation error is within ε. With ε = 0 this is Xu–Raginsky. With ε > 0 it stays finite where I(S;W) is infinite. For a Lipschitz loss R becomes the rate-distortion function of the output's marginal law, and as ε → 0 its rate-distortion dimension. A tail bound replaces I(S;W) by its supremum over laws within log(1/δ) in KL. Every bound depends on the unknown data distribution. | Read |
| [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md) v2 | Vereshchagin & Vitányi — Kolmogorov's structure functions and model selection | For a string x of length n and every complexity bound α, the minimal two-part code length λ_x(α), the structure function h_x(α) + α and the best achievable fit β_x(α) + K(x) are one function to within O(log n), and any set witnessing λ_x or h_x also witnesses β_x. Every non-increasing shape occurs for some x. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable but not computable; β_x is not even semicomputable. Finite sets only; the extension to computable distributions costs O(log n). | Read |
| [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md) v2 | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee — Information flow with hydrodynamic interactions | Two colloids are symmetrically coupled by the fluid, and the trap of one is moved by recorded Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise. Mutual information, its time-delayed form and transfer entropy recover the order drive → driven particle → other particle. Under moderate drive they also show some backflow, which disappears under strong drive (numerics only). Stronger coupling lowers the information the driven particle shares with the drive and raises what the particles share. Without the drive, the coupled particles are statistically independent. | Read |
| [NOTE-790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-790.md) | Vitányi — Meaningful Information | With total recursive functions as models, the shortest model that completes an optimal two-part code for a string (its sophistication) is a non-trivial split of its information into structure and noise. With partial recursive models the split collapses to zero for every string. The total-function, computable-distribution and finite-set classes agree to within logarithmic terms. Some strings of every length are almost all structure, and sophistication is not computable. | Read |
| [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md) | Barnett and Seth — Dynamical independence | A coarse-graining Y = f(X) is dynamically independent when the microscopic history adds nothing to predicting Y beyond Y's own history, given the environment: transfer entropy T(X → Y \| E) = 0. The condition is transformation-invariant and transitive. For linear state-space models it has a closed form, and it is minimized numerically over the Grassmannian. Generically no coarse-graining is exactly independent for VAR order above 1. The minima are many, and the authors treat them all as the "emergence portrait". | Read |
| [NOTE-801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-801.md) | Vitányi & Li — MDL induction, Bayesianism and Kolmogorov complexity | With the universal prior, the Fundamental Inequality puts −log Pr(D\|H) − log P(H) within α = K(Pr(·\|H)) + K(P) of K(D\|H) + K(H) when D is random for H and H is random for P. So ideal MDL and MAP agree to a factor 2^{−α} among such "admissible" hypotheses. α can be as large as K(H), and outside the admissible set the two can pick different hypotheses. For finite-set models, MAP, ideal MDL and Kolmogorov's minimal sufficient statistic coincide. | Read |
| [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md) | Goldwasser et al. — A Theory of Unsupervised Translation Motivated by Animal Communication | With a plausibility prior over the target language and no parallel data, maximum likelihood learns a translator whose error is bounded like a supervised Occam bound divided by the common ground. In the common-nonsense model err = O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))), tight up to a constant; in the knowledge-graph model more knowledge per node needs less agreement. Information-theoretic only, lossless, uniform languages. | Read |
| [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md) | Sefidgaran & Zaidi — Data-Dependent Generalization Bounds via Variable-Size Compressibility | If the number of codewords allowed for covering a block of experiments may depend on the realised sample and output, generalisation bounds can be data-dependent. The general bounds are change-of-measure inequalities that cover tail, PAC-Bayes and in-expectation forms. With the rate set to log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) for a fixed prior P, the tail bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. A new trajectory bound is data-dependent except for a coupling term, and its experiment drops that term. | Read |
| [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md) | Chowdhury et al. — Fundamental Limits of Perfect Concept Erasure | If an erased representation Z is independent of the concept A, it keeps at most I(Z;X) ≤ H(X\|A). A deterministic erasure reaches that only when the groups' distributions are permutations of one another. The paper says the bound is out of reach otherwise. That holds only for deterministic maps: a stochastic quantile coupling reaches it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Read |
| [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md) v2 | Belghazi et al. — Mutual Information Neural Estimation | Mutual information is the KL divergence of the joint from the product of marginals, and its Donsker–Varadhan dual is tight exactly at the log Radon–Nikodym derivative plus a constant. Maximizing that dual over a compact family of neural critics gives an estimator that is strongly consistent, for the exact empirical maximizer, on a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, with a uniform deviation bound of order d log d/ε² in the parameter count d. The mini-batch gradient is biased; a moving average is offered as a heuristic fix without proof. | Read |
| [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md) | Bach — Information Theory with Kernel Methods | With a continuous kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1 on a compact set, the uncentred covariance operator Σ_p is a density operator. Its quantum relative entropy is sandwiched between the KL of two kernel-smoothed distributions and the KL itself, D(p̃‖q̃) ≤ D(Σ_p‖Σ_q) ≤ D(p‖q), with equality on the right only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding. On the torus the gap is O(σ²) in the bandwidth. Kernel mutual information characterizes independence; conditional independence only one way. | Read |
| [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) | Goldreich — Foundations of Cryptography, Vol. 1 (1995 fragments): computational indistinguishability and pseudorandom generators | In the 1995 draft of Volume 1, computational indistinguishability is a strictly coarser equivalence than statistical closeness, and the book proves this two ways. Proposition 3.3 does it unconditionally: a counting argument shows there are ensembles supported on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform with gap 2^(−n/8) or more, but such an ensemble cannot be sampled efficiently. §3.3.1 shows that the output of any pseudorandom generator is statistically far from uniform yet, by definition, indistinguishable from it. That witness is efficiently samplable, and it needs pseudorandom generators, which exist if and only if one-way functions do (Theorem 3.29, stated without proof). That efficient post-processing preserves indistinguishability is set as Exercise 1 of §3.8.4, not proved in the text. All of this is asymptotic, about ensembles indexed by n, not about single pairs of distributions. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md) | Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin & Luby — A pseudorandom generator from any one-way function | There is a pseudorandom generator if and only if there is a one-way function (Theorem 6.2.2), in the uniform setting: adversaries are algorithms, and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine that turns an adversary for the constructed generator into an inverter for the given function. The route runs one-way function → false entropy generator → pseudoentropy generator → pseudorandom generator, where "computational entropy" is the Shannon entropy of some P-samplable distribution that no adversary of the given strength tells apart from the output. The general reduction is only weak-preserving: composed literally it needs seeds of length n^34, and the paper's direct construction n^10. The paper attributes to Goldreich [G : 89] the equivalence of pseudorandom generators with P-samplable pairs that are computationally indistinguishable but statistically very different; with Theorem 6.2.2 that gives the one-way function form, but the paper never writes that combined sentence. | Read |
| [NOTE-929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) | Alon & Klartag — optimal compression of approximate inner products | Storing every inner product and squared distance of n points of norm at most 1 in R^k to additive error ε takes Θ(n log n/ε²) bits once k ≥ log n/ε², Θ(nk log(2 + log n/(ε²k))) for log n ≤ k ≤ log n/ε², and Θ(nk log(1/ε)) below, for 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1. Comparing these counts across dimensions shows that some n points in R^k cannot be mapped into fewer than Ω(min{k, log(2 + ε²n)/ε²}) dimensions with additive error ε, for every ε ≥ 2/√n. A bipartite version of the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma reaches O(log(2 + ε²n)/ε²) dimensions; the one-family version at that size is left open. | Read |
| [NOTE-934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-934.md) | Barnett, Barrett and Seth — Granger causality and transfer entropy are equivalent for Gaussian variables | For jointly Gaussian stationary processes X, Y and Z, Geweke's Granger causality F_{Y→X\|Z} = ln(\|Σ(X\|X⁻⊕Z⁻)\|/\|Σ(X\|X⁻⊕Y⁻⊕Z⁻)\|) equals twice the transfer entropy T_{Y→X\|Z}, for multivariate predictor, predictee and conditioning variables (Eq. 13). The proof: OLS residual covariance is the partial covariance Σ(X\|Y), and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is ½ln\|Σ(X\|Y)\| + ½n ln(2πe). The authors keep G-causality apart from physically instantiated causation. | Read |
| [NOTE-936](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-936.md) | Williams and Beer — Nonnegative decomposition of multivariate information | Redundancy is I_min(S; A₁…A_k) = Σ_s p(s) min_i I(S = s; A_i), the expected minimum specific information. Restricted to antichains of sources and ordered by α ≼ β iff every source of β contains one of α, the collections form a lattice. The Möbius inverse of I_min on it gives partial-information atoms that are nonnegative (Theorem 5) and sum to I(S; R). Interaction information is synergy minus redundancy for three variables and a signed mixture for four, which explains its negativity and its +1 bit for both 3-parity and three copies. | Read |
| [NOTE-937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-937.md) | Bertschinger, Rauh, Olbrich, Jost and Ay — Quantifying unique information | For a target X and sources Y, Z, the unique information of Y is UĨ(X : Y \ Z) = min over Q ∈ Δ_P of MI_Q(X : Y \| Z), where Δ_P is the set of joints with the same (X,Y) and (X,Z) marginals. If unique information should depend only on those marginals, this is an upper bound on any such measure, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds. It is zero exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient. The measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate PI axioms and the identity property, and are a convex programme, but are bivariate only. | Read |
| [NOTE-938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md) | Kraskov, Stögbauer and Grassberger — Estimating mutual information | Two k-nearest-neighbour estimators of mutual information, I⁽¹⁾ and I⁽²⁾ (Eqs. 8–9), from the Kozachenko–Leonenko entropy estimate (Eq. 20) taken at one length scale in the joint and marginal spaces, so that the biases largely cancel. The only approximation is a locally constant density. Numerically the systematic error scales with k/N and vanishes for independent variables, a conjecture without proof; the ordered Weinman exponential is the one case where the stronger form fails. Extensions to multi-information (Eqs. 23, 30). Conditional mutual information is not treated. | Read |
| [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) | Massey — Causality, feedback and directed information | The textbook DMC, P(y^N\|x^N) = Π P(y_n\|x_n), is the DMC used without feedback; the right definition is P(y_n\|x^n y^{n−1}) = P(y_n\|x_n). Directed information I(X^N→Y^N) = Σ I(X^n; Y_n \| Y^{n−1}) is at most I(X^N;Y^N), equal without feedback (Theorem 1), and in a causal system bounds what the output says about the source (Theorem 3), so feedback cannot raise DMC capacity. Statistical dependence has no direction; directed information does. | Read |
| [NOTE-940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md) | Schreiber — Measuring information transfer | Defines transfer entropy T_{J→I} as the Kullback entropy between I's transition probabilities with and without J's past, at history lengths k for I and l for J (Eq. 4), which is the conditional mutual information I(i_{n+1}; j_n^{(l)} \| i_n^{(k)}). It is directional and ignores static correlation. A kernel estimator is proposed. Tent-map and Ulam-map lattices show it detecting the coupling direction where time-delayed mutual information fails; a heart–breath pair shows an asymmetry that the author says a common trigger could also explain. | Read |
| [NOTE-942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md) | Williams and Beer — Generalized measures of information transfer | With the I_min partial information decomposition, transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t \| X_t) is the unique information of Y_t about X_{t+1} (state-independent transfer, SITE) plus the synergy of X_t and Y_t (state-dependent transfer, SDTE). SITE alone suffices for perfect open-loop controllability (Theorem 1). Time-delayed mutual information is SITE plus redundancy. Two-source transfer splits into unique, redundant and synergistic parts. On a sleep-apnoea recording, heart→breath transfer is all SDTE. | Read |
| [NOTE-943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md) | Lizier, Prokopenko and Zomaya — Local information transfer as a spatiotemporal filter | Transfer entropy is the expectation of a local transfer entropy, t_{Y→X}(n+1, k, l) = log p(x_{n+1} \| x⁽ᵏ⁾_n, y⁽ˡ⁾_n)/p(x_{n+1} \| x⁽ᵏ⁾_n), defined at every point and possibly negative. Apparent transfer entropy conditions on the destination's past; complete transfer entropy also on its other causal parents. On elementary cellular automata, with k ≥ 6 (rule 110) and k = 16, local transfer entropy highlights gliders and domain walls as the dominant information-transfer structures; k = 1 and local time-lagged mutual information do not. The averages carry none of this. | Read |
| [NOTE-944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-944.md) | Harder, Salge and Polani — A bivariate measure of redundant information | I_min gives 1 bit of redundancy to two independent bits copied into the target, because it compares amounts of specific information and not their direction in the space of distributions over the target. The paper adds an identity axiom, I∩((X,Y); X, Y) = I(X; Y), and defines a bivariate I_red: project each posterior p(z\|x) onto the convex hull of the other source's posteriors, count what survives, take the smaller direction. I_red satisfies all four axioms and gives a nonnegative PID. It agrees with I_min except where I_min overstates redundancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-945](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md) | James, Barnett and Crutchfield — Information flows? A critique of transfer entropies | Information flow from X to Y is information in Y attributable solely to X's past. Transfer entropy is not it. For Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1} it is 1 bit, but the bit is synergistic, carried by both pasts jointly (co-information −1). For Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1} both transfer entropies are 0, and the causation entropies (conditional transfer entropies) are 1 bit each, again localizing a joint bit. By PID, transfer entropy is unique plus synergistic information; conditioning adds synergy, it does not only remove redundancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) | Ay and Polani — Information flows in causal networks | In a finite causal Bayesian network, X_B is causally independent of X_A imposing X_S if setting x_A after setting x_S leaves X_B's post-interventional distribution unchanged. For every model on a DAG this holds iff every directed path from A to B meets S (ud-separation, Theorem 2). Information flow I(X_A → X_B \| X̂_S) is conditional mutual information with interventional probabilities in place of observational ones, zero under causal independence. Examples show it can differ from conditional mutual information and from transfer entropy in either direction. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1, by the reading's check. | Read |
